name: End the session and return to the login screen
priorityReason: Ships with login. Every signed-in actor uses it, and shared devices make it a safeguarding matter.

goal.capability: to end my session from any screen
goal.outcome: nobody can use my account on a shared device after I leave

primaryActor: Every actor who can sign in — Super Admin, School Admin, Accounts, Staff, Coordinator, Principal, Teacher, Student, Parent / Guardian, Driver.

additional.description: The session passes the idle timeout set by the password policy and is ended in the same way.

postConditions: The session is invalidated on the server. Any token issued from it is dead, so a copy retained elsewhere cannot be replayed.
No protected page is reachable from this device until the actor signs in again, whether by the back button or by a direct address.
Client-side session storage is cleared, so nothing about the actor remains on a shared device.
The sign-out is recorded in the audit log, marked as explicit or as an idle timeout.
Any other session the same actor holds — another device, or the driver app — remains active and untouched.
Unsaved form data is discarded, except where a use case defines a draft state.
No student, staff, fee or academic record changes.

entities.notes: Invalidated server-side, not only cleared in the browser.
Records the sign-out and whether it was explicit or caused by the idle timeout.

permissions.notes: No actor can sign another out. Withdrawing an account is suspension, which is role and account management.

businessRules.rule: The session is invalidated on the server, not only in the browser. A token retained from before sign-out must not work afterwards.
After sign-out no protected page is reachable, including by the browser back button or by typing the address directly.
A session left idle past the timeout set by the password policy is ended automatically, in the same way and with the same audit entry, marked as a timeout rather than an explicit sign-out.
Unsaved form data is discarded without a prompt, except where a use case defines a draft state.
Signing out of the driver app ends the driver session only, and has no effect on any main-system session held by the same person.
Every sign-out is written to the audit log.

transitions.condition: Sign out is selected in the header.

basicFlow.navigation: Any authenticated screen → Header → Sign out
basicFlow.userAction: Selects the sign-out control in the header.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Clears client-side session storage and writes the audit entry.
Returns the actor to the login screen. No protected page is reachable afterwards, by the back button or by a direct address.

alternateFlows.condition: The session reached the idle timeout rather than the actor signing out
alternateFlows.behaviour: The same steps run automatically. The audit entry records a timeout rather than an explicit sign-out, and the login screen explains that the session ended (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The actor is signed in to the driver app
alternateFlows.navigation: Driver app → Sign out → Driver login screen
alternateFlows.behaviour: The driver session ends. Any main-system session held by the same person is unaffected (BR-5).

exceptions.systemResponse: Treated as success. The actor reaches the login screen either way.
Client-side session data is cleared immediately and the server session is invalidated on next contact.
exceptions.messageShown: You have been signed out on this device.

exceptions.condition: A protected page is requested after sign-out
exceptions.systemResponse: The request is refused and the actor is returned to the login screen.
exceptions.messageShown: Your session has ended. Please sign in again.

acceptanceCriteria.given: A signed-in actor on any screen
acceptanceCriteria.then: they reach the login screen and the browser back button reaches no protected page

acceptanceCriteria.given: A session token captured before sign-out
acceptanceCriteria.when: it is replayed against any protected endpoint

acceptanceCriteria.given: A session left idle past the timeout
acceptanceCriteria.when: the actor returns to the tab
acceptanceCriteria.then: they see the login screen and the audit log records the end as a timeout, not an explicit sign-out

acceptanceCriteria.given: A Driver signed in to the driver app and also to the main system
acceptanceCriteria.when: they sign out of the driver app
acceptanceCriteria.then: the main-system session is still active
it holds the actor, the time and whether the end was explicit or a timeout

useCases.name: Login
useCases.why: A session must exist to end.

masterData: Idle timeout setting in the password policy

outOfScope.item: The idle timeout value itself, which the password policy owns

openQuestions.question: Should signing out end the actor's sessions on their other devices as well?
What is the idle timeout, and does it differ by role?
openQuestions.assumption: One value for all roles, set in the password policy. The value is not yet specified.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
